title: Inner Landscapes: A Pulse Reading of MacArthur Park
description: A collaborative pulse reading of MacArthur Park, Los Angeles, developed through installation, archives, sculptural construction, and practices of care.
collaborators: Cloud6 with Jane Zhang, Enoch Ma, and Han Jik Kim

gallery.caption: Knoll / Clinic, installation view, Inner Landscapes. Goethe-Institut Los Angeles Project Space, 2025–26.

details: Inner Landscapes: A Pulse Reading of MacArthur Park brings together different ways of studying, experiencing, and tending to an urban landscape. Developed through Cloud6, the project approaches MacArthur Park through the language of the body—not as a single diagnosis, but through overlapping histories, material encounters, and forms of observation.
image_alt: Knoll installation inside the Inner Landscapes exhibition

sections.heading: A park with many interiors
sections.body: MacArthur Park has been described as a lung of Los Angeles, divided by an intervention likened to urban surgery, and repeatedly diagnosed through the language of urban health and disorder. Inner Landscapes takes these descriptions seriously as ways of seeing that can shape what happens to a place. Rather than supplying one authoritative diagnosis, the work gathers different forms of knowledge into a collective reading.

sections.heading: Pulse as a way of looking
sections.body: The project draws on acupuncture and pulse reading alongside archival research, material experiments, and lived relationships to MacArthur Park. The exhibition brings together ways of sensing a landscape that do not necessarily agree with one another. Its methods unfold through encounters, objects, and the people who make and use them.

sections.heading: Knoll / Clinic
sections.body: The Knoll / Clinic extends the practice of acupuncture into the installation, connecting the landscape of the park with a space for bodily care. Developed with Han Jik Kim, an acupuncturist, the clinic is not simply a representation of healing: community acupuncture sessions make care one of the ways the project is enacted.

sections.heading: Other parts of the landscape
sections.body: Bridge, developed with Enoch Ma, translates questions of labor, exposure, dependency, and endurance into an assemblage of lumber-cart frames, steel, chains, and rust. Net, developed with Jane Zhang, works through historical and municipal languages surrounding the park. Other elements—including Sails, Lake, Faultlines, and Color Pathology—bring additional material and interpretive routes into the installation.

sections.heading: A collective reading
sections.body: Inner Landscapes was made through Cloud6 (Lauren Kim and Jane Zhang), in collaboration with Enoch Ma and Han Jik Kim. It was presented at the Goethe-Institut Los Angeles Project Space from November 2025 to January 2026. This entry is a starting record; additional photographs, archival documents, and component-specific notes can be added here as the archive grows.
